A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2C-Insert research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the relocated checklist and renumbered supplementary sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original L2C-Insert experiments on synthetic and benchmark TSP/CVRP instances, with component ablations and hyperparameter studies in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V3 retains these original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and hyperparameter studies. Results retained from v2 still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The architecture, insertion-position policy, supervised loss, node-selection rules, and local reconstruction procedure are retained. Appendices K–L explain the existing target construction and loss; the CVRP optimizer revision concerns experimental training settings.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic TSP/CVRP coverage from 100 to 100K nodes and the same TSPLIB and CVRPLIB Set-X instances. No additional task, domain, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding benchmark and ablation tables. The expanded discussions of PolyNet and Neural Deconstruction Search do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the reported CVRP training configuration from Adam for 50 epochs to AdamW for 15 epochs, substantially revising its training budget and optimizer. TSP remains at Adam for 50 epochs. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the earlier description was corrected.

E4.justification: The ablations, hyperparameter studies, and visualization cases are retained. Appendix F revisits the existing Table 4 experiment; Appendix H derives per-instance timings from existing measurements without adding an ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both checklists disclose seed 123 for training/inference and explicitly report no statistical-significance analysis. Neither version adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or error bars.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation table values are retained. Section 4.1 corrects the CVRP1K speedup over LEHD from 8.7× to 2×, consistent with Table 1's unchanged 4.15-hour and 2.05-hour runtimes. New Table 14 derives per-instance TSP times of 2.9, 21.8, 62.4, and 97.8 seconds. V3 also newly describes AdamW as more stable.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds an asymptotic complexity derivation: O(n^3 d) for full construction under both heavy-decoder paradigms and approximately O(k^2 d) per insertion step with neighborhood restriction. Existing mathematical formulations and numbered equations remain unchanged; the target-position clarification restates the existing construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same learning-driven insertion contribution, three framework components, and TSP/CVRP performance and scalability claims. Appendix I elaborates their positioning without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly identifies fixed greedy node selection as a limitation and proposes learned selection and hybrid append/insert models. Section 4 qualifies training labels as potentially near-optimal. New appendices clarify runtime comparisons, construction versus refinement, computational tradeoffs, and the loss rationale, while retaining the principal result interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 promises code and trained models upon acceptance; v3 supplies a repository address and changes the access checklist answer to Yes. Table 13 additionally documents baseline iteration and reviser configurations, and Section 4 revises CVRP training details. The PDFs establish these access disclosures, not independent verification of the repository contents.

R1.justification: V3 adds Neural Deconstruction Search and distinguishes its learned removal and rule-based reinsertion from learned insertion. It expands discussion of previously cited PolyNet, adds recent routing/LLM and AdamW references, and clarifies its relationship to traditional insertion heuristics and neighborhood search. The central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: New Appendices F–L substantially expand explanations of search, computational budgets, timing, positioning, complexity, targets, and loss. The checklist moves before the appendices, and former Appendices F–I become M–P. Main-text editing is more localized, including expanded limitations, acknowledgments, and affiliation updates.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 13–14 for baseline settings and timing breakdowns, expands Table 1's caption, and renumbers the license table from 13 to 15. The six figures and existing experimental tables retain their displays with limited formatting and reflow changes. New Table 14 has the unfinished caption 'Add caption'.

improvement.justification: The corrected speedup, clearer runtime accounting, more explicit limitations, and reported code/model access improve accuracy and reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by the unexplained CVRP training revision alongside unchanged scores and Appendix L's misleading implication that a tiny softmax target probability necessarily produces very large parameter gradients. The net improvement is useful but limited.
